text:
sasha: Nightly intake — CVE feed flagged three deps with public exploit chatter: pyyaml, okhttp, kms-client. Can we do a rapid initial triage? Who can pick up pyyaml? Need EPSS/CVSS, exploitability notes, RBAC/KMS impact, and whether audit logs expose anything. @raj?

sec-bot: New feed: CVE-2026-1423 (pyyaml) — EPSS=0.72, CVSS=9.8 (RCE). PoC seen in the wild. https://vulnfeed.example/CVE-2026-1423 :eyes:

raj: I'll take pyyaml. Quick heads-up: I can repro a PoC against 5.4.1 in our staging container. I'll run an SBOM sweep across services and list owners.

raj: ```
# local SBOM sweep
sbom-scan --artifact services/* --dep pyyaml==5.4.1 
# results: inference-runtime, model-server, devex-utils
```

olivia: I'll grab okhttp (CVE-2026-0899) — EPSS lower but exploit requires specific TLS proxy config. Checking if our mobile SDK or server-side clients use the affected code paths.

jamie-oncall: kms-client question: is the vuln in aws/gcp client lib or our internal kms-wrapper? If client-side parsing, maybe we only need logging/audit changes, not key rotation.

devon: kms-client looks like a client parsing bug. Does not directly leak key material in normal flow, but malformed requests can cause the SDK to surface wrapped key bytes into error payloads. If we log request/response bodies without redaction we could leak. Recommend restricting `kms:Decrypt` principal list and verify logs.

sasha: Action items: raj -> patch/PR for pyyaml, add unit test, plan canary for model-server. olivia -> impact assessment for okhttp and mobile. devon -> audit logging & KMS policy review. jamie -> open SEC ticket and tag owners for rotation if needed.

raj: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference/commit/abc123 — backported patch to 5.4.2. Added a regression unit test. Will request quick review (cc @olivia for release window).

olivia: Noted. Mobile SDK not affected. Server-side model-server is. Plan: canary 2% -> 20% over 2 hours. Run smoke tests for inference correctness and latency.

jamie-oncall: Created SEC-5412 to track: triage notes, EPSS/CVSS values, owners, RBAC checklist, audit-redaction task, and rollback plan. Adding @dev-team and @infra.

devon: Suggested RBAC snippet to tighten KMS Decrypt:```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/CMK-EXAMPLE"],
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalTag/team": "inference"}}
    }
  ]
}
```

devon: Also: audit logs show `body` logging enabled for model-server-prod-1 and analytics-ingest. We should stop logging full request bodies immediately and run a redaction sweep.

sec-bot: Audit monitor flagged verbose body logs for services: model-server-prod-1, analytics-ingest. Created task LOG-208 to remove sensitive body logging and rotate any keys found in logs.

sasha: Triage priority: pyyaml -> P0 (active exploit), okhttp -> P2, kms-client -> P1 (potential audit leakage). EPSS/CVSS recorded in SEC-5412.

raj: Can we do a hotfix deploy tonight? I need approval for a short elevated CIDR allowlist for canary traffic and a rapid rollback path.

olivia: :thumbsup: I'll be available at 23:00 for the deploy window and can run canary checks.

jamie-oncall: I'll monitor post-deploy: watch for anomalous `kms:Decrypt` attempts and any unexpected 5xxs. If we see suspicious decrypts or leaked keys, we'll rotate CMKs and rollback.

sasha: Thanks team. Checklist in SEC-5412: PR, canary plan, rollback, key rotation readiness, audit redaction, changelog. Update ticket with outcomes and close this thread after post-deploy checks.
